title: Majestic Interference: Choose the Unblocked Promotion
summary: After either capture of the sacrificed rook, promote on the line blocked by Black’s own piece.

nodes.question: The rook captured on d5. Which pawn can promote safely?
nodes.explanation: Rd5 blocks Bf3’s diagonal to a8. The d-pawn is still stopped by the rook on its file, so White should promote the a-pawn.

nodes.question: The bishop captured on d5. Does the same pawn promote?
nodes.explanation: Bd5 blocks Rd2’s file toward d8. The bishop still sees a8, so this time White should promote the d-pawn.

branches.title: Rook capture: promote the a-pawn
commentary: This is the complete seven-piece position after the source’s ...Rxd5. The preceding eight-piece Rd5 sacrifice is context outside exact verification.

a8=Q promotes safely because Rd5 interrupts Bf3–e4–d5–c6–b7–a8. White retains an exact win with the remaining d7 and h7 pawns preserved. The queen-versus-rook-and-bishop conversion is not presented as immediate mate.
branches.explanation: a8=Q promotes safely because Rd5 interrupts Bf3–e4–d5–c6–b7–a8. White retains an exact win with the remaining d7 and h7 pawns preserved. The queen-versus-rook-and-bishop conversion is not presented as immediate mate.

branches.title: Bishop capture: promote the d-pawn
commentary: Switch to the separately illustrated seven-piece position after ...Bxd5. These two capture outcomes are separate nodes, not a continuous move sequence.
d8=Q promotes safely because Bd5 blocks Rd2’s d-file. White retains an exact win against rook, bishop and h7 pawn, with a7 still present. The correct pawn changes when the blocking piece changes.
branches.explanation: d8=Q promotes safely because Bd5 blocks Rd2’s d-file. White retains an exact win against rook, bishop and h7 pawn, with a7 still present. The correct pawn changes when the blocking piece changes.

branches.title: Independent error: push into the rook’s file
commentary: Independently compare the other promotion after ...Rxd5. This error is not shown as a source continuation.
d8=Q gives up the win and loses. Rd5 still has a clear path up the d-file; it is the bishop’s diagonal that has been obstructed.
Rxd8+ captures the new queen with check along the eighth rank. White cannot immediately answer by promoting a8 because its king is in check. The exact resulting position is a White loss.

branches.explanation: Rxd8+ captures the new queen with check along the eighth rank. White cannot immediately answer by promoting a8 because its king is in check. The exact resulting position is a White loss.

branches.title: Independent error: push into the bishop’s diagonal
commentary: Independently compare the wrong promotion after ...Bxd5. The capture sequence demonstrates how removing the blocker restores the second defender.
a8=Q loses: Bd5 still controls a8 along c6 and b7.
Bxa8 takes the queen and leaves the d-file. Rd2 is no longer obstructed by its own bishop.
d8=Q tries the remaining promotion, but the rook now has a clear file to d8.
Rxd8+ takes the second queen with check. Both pawns have disappeared, and White’s bare king faces rook, bishop and h7 pawn in an exact losing ending.

exercises.prompt: Why does the rook on d5 help the a-pawn?
exercises.answer: It blocks its own bishop’s diagonal from f3 to a8. The same rook still stops d8, so choose a8=Q.

exercises.prompt: Why do the roles reverse when the bishop takes on d5?
exercises.answer: The bishop blocks its rook’s d-file, freeing d8. Its own diagonal to a8 remains open, so promoting a8 would let it capture.

startContext: Two separately illustrated seven-piece positions are checked: after ...Rxd5 at 93 seconds, and after ...Bxd5 at 97 seconds. White’s preceding Rh5+/Rd5 interference belongs to the larger eight-piece source setup and is not certified here. These selected continuations teach which promotion works after each capture, with independent wrong-pawn comparisons. They do not establish the soundness or uniqueness of the earlier rook sacrifice.
